statement.p: Use the Divergence Theorem to calculate the flux of \mathbf{F} across S, where \mathbf{F}=5x^{2}yz\boldsymbol{i}+2xy^{2}z\boldsymbol{j}+1xyz^{2}\boldsymbol{k}\ and S is the surface of the box enclosed by the planes x=0,x=1,y=0,y=2,z=0 and z=2.

static.solution:
{\rm div}\ \mathbf{F} = \frac {\delta}{\delta x}(5 x^2 y z)\mathbf{i} + \frac {\delta}{\delta y}(2 x y^2 z)\mathbf{j} + \frac {\delta}{\delta z}(1 x y z^2)\mathbf{k} = 10xyz+4xyz+2xyz = 10xyz+4xyz+2xyz, so by the Divergence Theorem,
\int\int_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \ d \mathbf{S} = \int\int\int_E {\rm div}\ \mathbf{F}\ dV = \int_0^{1}\int_0^{2}\int_0^{2} 10xyz+4xyz+2xyz \ dz\ dy\ dx = 16\int_0^{1} x\ dx\int_0^{2} y\ dy\int_0^{2} z\ dz = 16\lbrack\frac 1 2 x^2\rbrack_0^{1} \lbrack\frac 1 2 y^2\rbrack_0^{2} \lbrack\frac 1 2 z^2\rbrack_0^{2} = 16(\frac 1 2 1)(2)(2) = 32
